newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislator seeks boost in school technology.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislator seeks boost in school technology.

text.p: A California state legislator on Friday said he introduced a bill to bring every high school classroom in the state online by the year 2000. Republican Assemblyman Fred Aguiar said Assembly Bill 1011 would establish the so-called Digital High Schools initiative and ensure that every classroom in each of California's 840 high schools would have the use of up-to-date computer technology by 2000. Gov. Pete Wilson appropriated $50 million for the initiative in his 1997-98 budget plan, enough to fund the program for 100 schools in its first year, Aguiar said. The program would provide teachers and students with the use of educational software, word-processing programs and access to the Internet.

Schools would be connected to students' homes via electronic mail, allowing teachers to keep parents better informed of homework and classroom activities, Aguiar said.

"We must provide students with the opportunity to learn computer skills and to harness the capabilities of the Internet," the assemblyman said. "We owe it to our children to prepare them to compete in tomorrow's work environment."
